analysis.investment_thesis: Avax Apparels fails both pillars of the Magic Formula: a 0.33% ROE signals near-zero return on capital, while a 17.8x P/E implies an earnings yield of only ~5.6% — neither cheap nor good. This is a textbook "avoid" on a systematic basis.
key_strengths: Promoter holding at 51.98% provides majority control/skin-in-the-game
Small 34 Cr market cap leaves theoretical room for operational turnaround
Dual exposure (apparel + silver ornaments) offers minor diversification
key_risks: ROE of 0.33% means capital is essentially idle — fails ROIC hurdle badly
Earnings yield ~5.6% (1/17.8) is well below the 12%+ Magic Formula threshold
Micro-cap textile/jewellery trader with no visible moat and commoditised products
red_flags: ROE <1% suggests either near-zero profitability or bloated equity base
P/E of 17.8x on a microcap with negligible returns indicates speculative pricing
No EBIT/EV data disclosed — cannot verify true earnings quality
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula requires a company to be both cheap (high EBIT/EV) and good (high ROIC). Avax Apparels fails both tests decisively. ROE of 0.33% is effectively zero — a bank FD returns ~20x more on capital — meaning the business is not generating meaningful economic returns. At a 17.8x P/E, the earnings yield is roughly 5.6%, well below the 12% threshold I look for, and actually below the risk-free rate in India. A company that is neither cheap nor productive has no place in a Magic Formula portfolio.

At a 34 Cr market cap, this is a micro-cap trader in commoditised apparel and silver ornaments with no evidence of pricing power, scale advantage, or capital discipline. Systematic ranking would place this stock in the bottom decile on both axes. I would pass without hesitation — there are hundreds of Indian small-caps with genuinely high ROIC at single-digit earnings multiples that deserve capital ahead of this one.
